test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Oct 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Infant Mortality Rate (or IMR) indicates the number of children that die before the age of ______ as a proportion of 1000 live children born in that particular year.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infant mortality rate**

 
 
• **It is the probability of a child born in a specific year or period dying before reaching the age of one if subject to age-specific mortality rates of that period. Hence, Option 3 is correct.**
 
• The infant mortality rate is strictly speaking not a rate (i.e. the number of deaths divided by the number of population at risk during a certain period of time) but a probability of death derived from a life table and expressed as a rate per 1000 live births.
 
• In accordance with the **UN** **Millenium Development Goals (MDG),** the goal was to cut down child mortality rate by two-thirds from 1995 to 2015.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In India, it **declined** considerably at the rate of almost **57%.** The IMR came down from** 80** infant deaths per 1000 live births (in **1995**) to **33** deaths per 1,000 live births (in** 2017: according to the SRS bulletin 2019**).
 
• **IMR** has 2 components:
 
 
• **IMR:** infants dying within 1 year of birth and,
 
• **Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR):** It is defined as the ‘number of deaths during the **first 28 completed days of life per 1,000** live births in a given year or period’.
 
 
 
• **Globally** according to **UNICEF**, NMR was **18 deaths per 1000** live births (in 2018), whereas, in **India,** NMR was** 23 deaths per 1000** live births **(approximately 7,000 newborn deaths every day).**
 
• The decline in NMR is at a very slow pace both globally and in India. It is almost one-third of the rate of decline of IMR.
